blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Reading a British dress code means watching two things at once: the office you are in, and the moment you are in. A client meeting may require a step up from an internal day. A visit to head office may be smarter than a visit to a regional one, and a finance review in front of the board is probably not the day for a bright tie.

Context matters more than any single rule. The quiet skill is to dress slightly better than the minimum the day demands — enough to show respect, but not so much that you stand out from your own team.

If in doubt, watch what the most senior woman or man in the room wears, and match that, half a step down. It rarely goes wrong.

items.q: According to the text, what two things should you watch at once?
options: The office you are in and the moment you are in
items.why: "watching two things at once: the office you are in, and the moment you are in."

items.q: What is described as "the quiet skill"?
options: Copying the most junior person in the room
Standing out from your own team
Dressing slightly better than the minimum the day demands
Wearing exactly what the rulebook states
items.why: "dress slightly better than the minimum the day demands — enough to show respect."

items.q: The text suggests that a board review is…
options: the same as a regional visit
probably not the day for a bright tie
the best day to wear something eye-catching
less formal than an internal day
items.why: "a finance review in front of the board is probably not the day for a bright tie."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The right choice depends on the day, not only the office.
You should calibrate from the most senior person present.
A single fixed rule matters more than context.
It is safer to be slightly more formal than too casual.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que "context matters more than any single rule" — o oposto da opção 0.

items.q: The advice to match the senior person "half a step down" suggests that you should…
options: stay close to their level, but a touch less formal
dress more formally than the most senior person
ignore what others in the room are wearing
always wear the most casual option available
items.why: Inferência: "half a step down" indica ficar perto do nível do sênior, porém um pouco abaixo — sem ofuscar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte orientando um novo gerente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, next week you're going up to the head office in Mayfair for the first time. It's the traditional one, and it reads a little differently from our floor here, so let me give you a steer.

Honestly, don't overthink it, but do read the day. It's an internal review, not a client pitch, so you don't need to go all the way up. A well-cut suit, plain shirt, and I'd leave the brighter ties at home — that building is quite conservative, and you don't want to be the one thing people remember.

Here's the trick I always use. When you walk in, have a quiet look at whoever is the most senior person in the room, and just settle half a step below that. If they're in a dark suit, you're fine in a slightly softer one. You'll blend in, which is exactly what you want on a first visit.

And look, if you're ever unsure, err on the smarter side. Nobody has ever been quietly judged for being a fraction too tidy. It's the other way round that gets noticed.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where is the new manager going next week?
options: The traditional head office in Mayfair
items.why: "next week you're going up to the head office in Mayfair for the first time."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say he does NOT need to "go all the way up"?
options: It is an internal review, not a client pitch
He will not meet anyone senior
items.why: "It's an internal review, not a client pitch, so you don't need to go all the way up."

items.q: What is the "trick" Charlotte recommends?
options: Ask the reception what to wear
Settle half a step below the most senior person in the room
Match the most junior person present
Wear the brightest tie he owns
items.why: "settle half a step below that" — calibrar pela pessoa mais sênior.

items.q: Charlotte's comment about the bright ties suggests that the head office is…
options: conservative, where standing out is unwise
items.why: Inferência: "that building is quite conservative" e o conselho de guardar as gravatas chamativas apontam para um ambiente sóbrio.

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "It's the other way round that gets noticed"?
options: Being under-dressed is what people notice and judge
The seating order is what matters most
Arriving late is the real problem
Being too smart draws unwanted attention
items.why: Inferência: se estar um pouco arrumado demais nunca é criticado, então é o contrário — estar informal demais — que chama atenção negativa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A client meeting usually requires a step up from an internal day." A step up here means…
options: a move to a higher, more formal level
items.why: Step up = subir um nível: aqui, um grau mais formal do que um dia interno.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The visit to ___ in Mayfair felt more formal than any regional branch."
items.why: Head office = matriz — a sede em Mayfair, contrastada com uma filial regional.

items.q: "He didn't want to stand out on his first visit." To stand out means to…
options: be noticeably different from the others
items.why: Stand out = destacar-se, chamar atenção por ser diferente dos demais.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A ___ in front of the directors is not the moment for a bright tie."
items.why: Board review = revisão da diretoria — um momento sóbrio, sem roupa chamativa.

items.q: "If in doubt, watch the senior person and match their level." To match here means to…
items.why: To match = combinar, alinhar-se ao mesmo nível da pessoa de referência.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre etiqueta e ambiente de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "When in doubt, err on the side of being slightly smarter." This means to…
options: choose the safer, more cautious option
items.why: Err on the side of = pender para o lado mais seguro/cauteloso da escolha.

items.q: "Before the visit, Charlotte gave him a quiet heads-up about the dress code." A heads-up is…
items.why: Heads-up = um aviso ou dica antecipada para preparar a pessoa.

items.q: "On a first visit, it's smart to blend in rather than stand out." To blend in means to…
options: dress far more formally than everyone
fit in with the group without drawing attention
items.why: Blend in = misturar-se ao grupo, passar despercebido, sem chamar atenção.

items.q: "Don't overthink it — just read the day and calibrate." To overthink means to…
options: consider something far more than necessary
items.why: Overthink = pensar demais, complicar algo que é simples.

items.q: "He decided to play it safe and wear a plain dark suit." To play it safe means to…
options: avoid risk by choosing the reliable option
items.why: Play it safe = jogar pelo seguro, optar pela escolha de menor risco.
